text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended on Friday.

LONDON - The UK's leading FTSE 100 share index ended on a stronger note, tracking Wall Street higher after the latest U.S. inflation figures eased fears of a near-term U.S. interest rate hike. The blue chip index, which spent most of the session struggling in negative territory, cleared the 4,400 hurdle late in the session and ended 26.6 points higher at 4,424.3, rising four points from Friday week.

FRANKFURT - German shares reverse course to close bourse trade higher despite Wall Street tumble, with buying interest still alive on the domestic side, but volumes modest and market eyeing U.S. data. The DAX index closed up 9.48 points at 3,359.29, down 60.22 from last week. In post-bourse trade the DAX index stood at 3,404.29.

PARIS - French stocks closed higher on a sharper than expected fall in U.S. producer prices that quelled fears of an imminent rise in U.S. interest rates. The blue-chip CAC-40 index finished up 13.52 points or 0.51 percent to 2,645.62, down 62.66 from last Friday.
ZURICH - Swiss shares ended firmer and near the day's high after storming back from a slide of nearly 100 points.

"It was the biggest countermove I have ever seen," one trader said, adding that better-than-expected U.S. data and a recovery on Wall Street were instrumental in the late rise. The All-share Swiss Performance Index (SPI) was up 12.27 points or 0.42 percent at 2,934.97, a drop of 3.47 from the seventh of March.

TOKYO - Tokyo stocks closed slightly higher in a market that was relieved by a fairly smooth settlement of March Nikkei 225 stock futures and options contracts earlier in the day, but participants were still cautious, waiting for the government to unveil specific measures to boost land liquidity, which could help pep up Japan's sluggish economy. The Nikkei 225 average gained 23.16 points or 0.13 percent to finish at 17,923.64, a fall 275.10 from seven days ago.

HONG KONG - Hong Kong stocks closed sharply lower, shaken by Wall Street's deep dive and the spectre of an uptrend in U.S. and local lending rates. The Hang Seng Index slid 180.56 points, or 1.40 percent to close at 12,736.53, falling 567.71 from last week.

SYDNEY - Australian shares ended sharply lower with the negative lead from nervous U.S. markets translating into losses across the board, in the face of a 2.3 percent drop in the Dow as U.S. investors fretted over potential interest rate hikes, sellers had control of the local market right from the outset with no sector escaping the axe.The All Ordinaries index shed 29.40 points to close at 2,423.20, down 15.30 on the week.

JOHANNESBURG - South African shares rode a United States-inspired roller coaster and ended firmly down after taking a knock from Thursday's huge fall on Wall Street, Dow Jones industrial shares shed 160 points in the fifth biggest points fall ever and the reaction was immediate upon South African shares as they tumbled, the drop had been triggered by a sudden bout of panic on the outlook for short-term U.S. interest rates. The All-share index dropped 44.5 points to 7,127.1, up 65.2 from last week, Industrials shed 46.9 points to end at 8,327.2, a rise of 75.6 on the week and the Gold index ended off 21.3 points to 1,408.3, down 8.3 from last Friday.
